title: Codebook wording review: Results for the institution as a whole
background:
Review round 4 of the codebook wording. You chose on 30 October that agents draft the missing value definitions and you review every wording slot here. This page covers **results for the institution as a whole**.

Each card is one codebook item. Open "Show the wording slots" to read them. Each slot is labelled with where its text came from:

- **Plan text**
- **New agent draft (round 4)**
- **Option text you chose in round 3**
- **Agent edit of the signed questionnaire**
- **Text you approved on 30 October**
- **Old production text (version 2.5): rewrite or delete**

Answer per item: approve all, approve with line-edits or deletions in the comments (by slot number), or ask for a redraft. Deletion is open only for old version-2.5 slots and for one slot of each overlap pair. The batch card at the top approves everything you leave unmarked. No recommendation is given on any wording.

New agent drafts carry a certainty mark; those marked **Needs your decision** rest on no ruling or text for some point.

items.title: has genai activity
items.situation:
Recorded per institution.

3 slots: 2 × plan text; 1 × text you approved on 30 October.
items.body:
**1. Rule** — Plan text, from the specification
Institution-level consolidation (Stage 6) applies the v2.6 consolidation rules as jev questions or deterministic rules: explicit relations before merging observations; distinct/unresolved relations never merge; institution-level `no` only with complete supplied context and no unresolved signal. An institution whose reviewed pages are all negative at confidence ≥ 0.8 gets `no` directly; the complete-context rule blocks `no` only when an unresolved signal remains (a low-confidence negative downgraded under R-081 counts as one). RC-D-002 row 6: Stage 6 becomes the X29 truth table, with these ruled components: `background_only` pages may sit in the institution `no` set (S2 b); any downgraded page counts as unresolved (r2#40); the bar is the chosen answer's probability ≥ 0.8 (r2#26); `yes` can come from any pipeline, `no` from web pages only, and AI-text results never count (r2#44, r2#15); any supported GenAI purchase record can give `yes`, while the evidence tier still shows it as commitment (C5 a); `not_assessable` is set mechanically only and does not block `no` (C1 a). Also: X30 with the shared relation list incl. `governs` (R-017, r2#22); X31 pooled evidence, split when too long (r2#6, C-004); A06 per r2#21; A07 with 9 counts per pipeline; X23 replaced by r2#27; unit-credit flag (r2#47). `unresolved` stays a coding value and is reported as `unknown` in published summaries (all-07 c); unresolved relations still never merge. Inside the institution-level rule both `unresolved` and `not_assessable` keep their current roles, and `not_assessable` stays out of the institution-rate base (O15). [wording: PI — RC-D-003 §10: the restated institution rule] [wording: PI — RC-D-002 row 6: the X29 truth-table text and the X30, X31, A06 and A07 definitions]

**2. Rule** — Plan text, from review round 1
Codebook table: `yes` if >= 1 supported `confirms_activity` page with a supported activity; `no` if every attempted page (incl. failed fetches and unfollowed links) ends in {no_genai, confirms_absence, event_only, other_body} at confidence >= 0.8 and no page is ambiguous, background_only or failed; otherwise `unclear`. Variant for PI: allow background_only in `no`.

**3. Rule** — Text you approved on 30 October
Inside the institution-level rule both keep their current roles, and `not_assessable` stays out of the institution-rate base (O15).

items.title: activity relation
items.situation:
Recorded per activity.

14 slots: 8 × new agent draft (round 4); 2 × plan text; 4 × option text you chose in round 3.
items.body:
**1. Value `same_activity`** — New agent draft (round 4)
The two activity records describe the same activity: the same action by the same actor on the same tool or instrument. Only records joined by this link are merged.
_Draft certainty: medium._ _Note: Direction: the pair is read in order (first record, second record); the reverse values make that order necessary (R3 activity-16 b), but no text says which record is 'first'._

**2. Value `component_of_program`** — New agent draft (round 4)
The first record's activity is a named component of the program in the second. Both stay separate activities, linked.
_Draft certainty: medium._ _Note: Direction: the pair is read in order (first record, second record); the reverse values make that order necessary (R3 activity-16 b), but no text says which record is 'first'._

**3. Value `has_component`** — New agent draft (round 4)
The first record describes a program, and the second record's activity is one of its named components. Both stay separate activities, linked.
_Draft certainty: medium._ _Note: Direction: the pair is read in order (first record, second record); the reverse values make that order necessary (R3 activity-16 b), but no text says which record is 'first'._

**4. Value `shared_participation`** — New agent draft (round 4)
The two records describe one joint action in which several bodies take part.
_Draft certainty: low._ **Needs your decision:** As within a page: no text defines this link or says whether it merges the two records. _Note: Direction: the pair is read in order (first record, second record); the reverse values make that order necessary (R3 activity-16 b), but no text says which record is 'first'._

**5. Value `governs`** — New agent draft (round 4)
The first record's activity is a policy or other governance instrument that sets rules for the activity in the second. When a pair fits both this link and a component link, this link is used.
_Draft certainty: medium._ _Note: Direction: the pair is read in order (first record, second record); the reverse values make that order necessary (R3 activity-16 b), but no text says which record is 'first'._

**6. Value `governed_by`** — New agent draft (round 4)
The second record's activity is a policy or other governance instrument that sets rules for the activity in the first. When a pair fits both this link and a component link, this link is used.
_Draft certainty: medium._ _Note: Direction: the pair is read in order (first record, second record); the reverse values make that order necessary (R3 activity-16 b), but no text says which record is 'first'._

**7. Value `distinct_action`** — New agent draft (round 4)
The two records describe different activities, and none of the other links applies. The value is stored with a rule note.
_Draft certainty: medium._ _Note: Direction: the pair is read in order (first record, second record); the reverse values make that order necessary (R3 activity-16 b), but no text says which record is 'first'._

**8. Value `unresolved`** — New agent draft (round 4)
The sources do not settle whether the two records describe the same activity. They are never merged.
_Draft certainty: high._ _Note: Direction: the pair is read in order (first record, second record); the reverse values make that order necessary (R3 activity-16 b), but no text says which record is 'first'._

**9. Rule** — Plan text, from review round 1
Every pair of activity observations is asked, including identical names; candidate pairs pre-filtered deterministically only to skip obviously distinct pairs (different activity_type and tool), never to merge.

**10. Rule** — Plan text, from the specification
One shared relation list serves within-page and cross-page links: same activity, component of program, has component, shared participation, governs, governed by, distinct (`distinct_action`), unresolved, plus not-an-activity within a page (r2#22; activity-16 b; all-11).

**11. Rule** — Option text you chose in round 3
Add "has component" and "governed by".

**12. Rule** — Option text you chose in round 3
Components stay separate activities; a governing policy is recorded as governing.

**13. Rule** — Option text you chose in round 3
Store the distinct value with a rule note.

**14. Long-page rule (split rule)** — Option text you chose in round 3
Split the pool so every part sees both activities.
